title: [clinic · EX-06] Null questions for a real corpus
body:
> **Exercise clinic.** One long-running thread per exercise. Ask here rather than opening a
> new thread — the answers accumulate where the next person will look for them.
>
> **Exercise:** [`EX-06` — Null questions for a real corpus](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/30-learning/exercises/ex-06-null-questions-for-a-real-corpus.md) · difficulty 🟡

## What this exercise asks

Read the exercise first; this thread is for when you are stuck, not instead of it.

## Three ways people get stuck on this one

**1.** Nulls that are off-topic. A question about the weather is trivially unanswerable and measures nothing. A good null names real entities and asks something the corpus does not contain.

**2.** Nulls at an unrealistic base rate. Balancing the classes flatters every threshold — that is precisely the bug in [#7](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/issues/7).

**3.** Nulls that are accidentally answerable, because the fact is present somewhere you did not check.

## How to ask here

Post the **numbers you got**, the **config that produced them**, and **what you already tried**.
A question with a measurement in it gets answered in one round trip; a question without one
takes three.

If you have finished it, post the write-up in **Show and Tell** with the
`[solution · EX-06]` prefix rather than here — this thread stays for people who are stuck.
